newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline easier, sellers eye backwardation.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline easier, sellers eye backwardation.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices were easier on Tuesday with weaker NYMEX unleaded, lengthy supplies and slack buying all adding pressure, traders said.
However, physical barge prices were slow to react to the downside with sellers, keen to lock in the advantage of the markets backwardation, reluctant to offer the market down.
"People are trying to catch the benefit of the backwardation into July so they are reluctant to offer it too low despite the lack of buyers," one traders said.
Rotterdam barges continued to hold a small premium to AR liftings. Running refinery material was traded and offered over at $187 a tonne with AR talked $184/$185 fob.
Weaker NYMEX unleaded futures was seen putting pressure on swaps. July swaps traded early at $181 but were talked $177/$179 in late business with August and September at the same level.
Talk of demand from Nigeria failed to boost a lengthy cargo market. Eurograde cargoes were valued around fob high +$2 equivalent to around $182 fob NWE.
Nigeria was reported to be ordering the immediate importation of 33 cargoes of petroleum products to end an acute fuel shortage in the country.

"The cargoes will come from Europe, especially Spain as well as other Africa countries," Ibrahim Abubakar, the managing director of the Pipelines and Products Marketing Company, a unit of the Nigerian National Petroleum Corp, told reporters in Lagos.

ADDAX Nigeria is reported to have bought several cargoes last week and one major refiner was seen looking to fill a large low-octane cargo out of Lavera though it was unclear whether this would head to Nigeria.
However, Spanish refiners said they had so far had little fresh enquiry for cargoes.
"We've had no nominations -- We bought last week for West Africa, not Nigeria and we certainly don't plan to produce anything extra for Nigeria," a trader at one major Spanish refiner said.
